items.title: Can you believe it? An investigation into the impact of retraction source credibility on the continued influence effect

judge.evidence_topic: The continued influence effect refers to the finding that people often continue to rely on misinformation in their reasoning even if the information has been retracted.
judge.evidence_empirical: In two experiments, we found that source trustworthiness but not source expertise indeed influences retraction effectiveness
judge.reason: O artigo investiga o efeito de influência continuada através de dois experimentos, atendendo aos critérios de estudo empírico e tema. O achado principal sobre a confiabilidade da fonte e a persistência do efeito é sustentado pelo resumo.

items.title: Failure to accept retractions: A contribution to the continued influence effect

judge.evidence_topic: Previous research has shown that when information about a narrative event is retracted, people continue to use that information even though it has been explicitly identified as incorrect. Experiment 3 modified the alternative account to increase plausibility, and added two additional stories/question sets to ensure effects were not limited to one set of materials.
judge.evidence_empirical: Experiment 1 assessed this using a continued influence effect paradigm with an additional probe asking whether participants believed the explicitly stated change. Experiment 2 included an additional explicit instruction that participants could say “don’t know” if they were unsure of how to respond. Experiment 3 modified the alternative account to increase plausibility, and added two additional stories/question sets to ensure effects were not limited to one set of materials.
judge.reason: O artigo é um estudo empírico (três experimentos) publicado em periódico revisado por pares dentro do período solicitado. O tema é o efeito de influência continuada (CIE) utilizando materiais neutros (histórias narrativas), sem viés político ou de saúde. Os métodos descritos no resumo coincidem com os dados extraídos, e o achado principal é sustentado pelo texto do resumo.

items.title: Is it smart to read on your phone? The impact of reading format and culture on the continued influence of misinformation

judge.evidence_topic: Participants read pairs of short newspaper-style articles containing a critical piece of information that was either retracted or not retracted, and were later assessed on their memory for critical and general details, as well as inferential judgements related to the retracted information.
judge.evidence_empirical: Participants read pairs of short newspaper-style articles containing a critical piece of information that was either retracted or not retracted, and were later assessed on their memory for critical and general details, as well as inferential judgements related to the retracted information.
judge.reason: O estudo utiliza um delineamento experimental com participantes humanos para investigar o efeito de influência continuada (CIE) através de textos estilo jornalístico, que são neutros e não abordam temas proibidos como política ou saúde. Os achados extraídos sobre o impacto do formato de leitura e da repetição da desinformação estão explicitamente presentes no resumo.

items.title: Mechanisms in continued influence: The impact of misinformation corrections on source perceptions

judge.evidence_topic: Research on the continued influence effect (CIE) of misinformation has demonstrated that misinformation continues to influence people’s beliefs and judgments even after it has been corrected.
judge.evidence_empirical: Study 1 demonstrated that an external correction (i.e., a new source labeling misinformation as false) influences perceptions of the misinformation source... Study 2 replicated the results of Study 1... Study 3 was a preregistered replication of previous results using new methodology.
judge.reason: O artigo descreve três estudos experimentais sobre o efeito de influência continuada (CIE). O achado principal está diretamente sustentado pelo resumo. O periódico (Memory & Cognition) e a natureza do estudo (mecanismos de percepção da fonte) indicam que o estudo é adequado ao escopo de experimentos neutros, não havendo menção a temas políticos ou de saúde.

items.title: How do forewarnings and post-warnings affect misinformation reliance? The impact of warnings on the continued influence effect and belief regression

judge.evidence_topic: The present study aimed to investigate these warnings’ effectiveness, depending on when they were given (either before or after misinformation).
judge.evidence_empirical: In two experiments (N = 337), we found that while a forewarning did reduce reliance on misinformation, retrospectively warned participants (when the warning was placed either between the misinformation and the retraction or just before testing) relied on the misinformation to a similar degree as unwarned participants.
judge.reason: O resumo descreve dois experimentos com participantes humanos sobre o efeito de influência continuada (CIE) e o uso de alertas, confirmando a metodologia e os achados extraídos sobre a redução inicial da dependência e a falta de durabilidade do efeito protetor.

items.title: The rational continued influence of misinformation
The inhibitory impact of collaboration on the continued influence effect of misinformation

judge.evidence_topic: The continued influence effect (CIE) of misinformation refers to the persistence of misinformation's impact on memory and inference even when individuals are aware of a retraction.
judge.evidence_empirical: This study examined whether collaborative processes affect the CIE and investigated the underlying mechanisms through three experiments.
judge.reason: O artigo investiga o efeito de influência continuada (CIE) através de três experimentos com participantes humanos, utilizando um paradigma de colaboração para avaliar a correção de desinformação. O estudo é empírico, publicado em periódico revisado por pares (Frontiers in Psychology) dentro do período solicitado, e não aborda temas proibidos (política, saúde, etc.). items.title: Vaccination against misinformation: The inoculation technique reduces the continued influence effect

judge.evidence_topic: Vaccination against misinformation: The inoculation technique reduces the continued influence effect

items.title: Exploring factors that mitigate the continued influence of misinformation

items.title: Cause typicality and the continued influence effect

judge.evidence_topic: In three experiments, we interrogated the importance of cause typicality for the generalizable utility of these correction strategies by manipulating the typicality of initial and alternative causes.

items.title: Comparing the use of open and closed questions for Web-based measures of the continued-influence effect

judge.evidence_topic: We compared the data quality obtained using open and closed response formats using the continued-influence effect (CIE), in which participants read a series of statements about an unfolding event, one of which is unambiguously corrected later.
judge.evidence_empirical: We implemented this basic procedure online (Exp. 1A, n = 78), comparing standard open-ended responses to an alternative procedure using closed-ended responses (Exp. 1B, n = 75). Finally, we replicated these findings in a larger preregistered study (Exps. 2A and 2B, n = 323).
judge.reason: O artigo investiga o efeito de influência continuada (CIE) utilizando cenários neutros (eventos fictícios), conduz experimentos com participantes humanos e os achados extraídos estão alinhados com o resumo.

judge.evidence_topic: The continued influence effect (CIE) refers to continued reliance on misinformation, even after it has been retracted.

items.title: Relative source credibility affects the continued influence effect: Evidence of rationality in the CIE

items.title: Executive function and the continued influence of misinformation: A latent-variable analysis

judge.evidence_topic: The current study investigated whether individual differences in EF could predict individual differences in CIE susceptibility.
judge.evidence_empirical: Participants completed several measures of EF subcomponents, including those of updating and inhibition, as well as set shifting, and a standard CIE task.

items.title: Examining the role of information integration in the continued influence effect using an event segmentation approach

judge.evidence_topic: Misinformation regarding the cause of an event often continues to influence an individual's event-related reasoning, even after they have received a retraction.
judge.evidence_empirical: Experiments 1 and 2 employed spatial event segmentation boundaries in an attempt to manipulate the ease with which a retraction can be integrated into a participant's mental event model.
judge.reason: O artigo investiga o efeito de influência continuada (CIE) por meio de experimentos comportamentais com cenários de eventos neutros, atendendo aos critérios de inclusão. judge.evidence_topic: Researchers Johnson and Seifert (1994, Experiment 1A) penned a seminal paper on this 'Continued Influence Effect' (CIE)... The present research investigated the direct replicability of their study with a French-speaking sample

items.title: Working memory capacity, removal efficiency and event specific memory as predictors of misinformation reliance

judge.evidence_topic: Event-related misinformation that has been retracted often continues to influence later reasoning regarding the event; this is known as the continued influence effect.
judge.evidence_empirical: The present study explored (1) whether memory for the materials more generally predicts continued influence, based on the notion that high-fidelity event representations may be easier to update, and (2) investigated the specific WM updating process of removal, testing whether participants’ ability to remove information from WM would predict their susceptibility to continued influence. Latent-variable modelling suggested that memory for the materials but not WM capacity and removal efficiency were significant predictors of continued influence.
judge.reason: O artigo investiga o efeito de influência continuada (CIE) utilizando materiais de eventos, o que se enquadra no recorte de neutralidade. O estudo é empírico, utiliza modelagem de variáveis latentes e o achado principal está corretamente descrito e sustentado pelo resumo.

items.title: Influence of individual differences in working memory on the continued influence effect of misinformation

judge.evidence_topic: The current research aimed to investigate whether the individual differences in the central executive function of WM and updating could influence the CIE of misinformation with varying relevance.
